definition: PATR-II is a linguistic formalism used in computational linguistics, developed by Stuart M.
details: Shieber. It uses context-free grammar rules and feature constraints on these rules.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. Think of it this way: PATR-II is a linguistic formalism used in computational linguistics, developed by Stuart M. And here is the clever part: Shieber. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. And that is PATR-II — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
